title: Liver failure
summary: Liver failure in the ICU: acute liver failure with King's College criteria, acute-on-chronic liver failure (EASL-CLIF and APASL), hepatic encephalopathy, ascites/SBP/hepatorenal syndrome, and coagulopathy of liver disease, with transplant referral throughout.

topics.title: Acute liver failure and King's College criteria
topics.summary: Recognise ALF, find the cause, give NAC, protect the brain, support organs and use King's College criteria for transplant referral.

definition.text: ALF = INR ≥ 1.5 with hepatic encephalopathy, without pre-existing cirrhosis, within 26 weeks of illness onset (EASL). Hyperacute (< 7 days jaundice-to-HE), acute (8-28 days), subacute (5-12 weeks). Hyperacute has highest cerebral oedema risk but best spontaneous survival.

steps.title: Confirm and grade
steps.detail: INR, bilirubin, glucose, lactate, ammonia, ABG, creatinine; grade HE (West Haven). Exclude cirrhosis (history, imaging).

steps.title: Find the cause
steps.detail: Paracetamol level, viral serology (HAV IgM, HEV IgM, HBsAg/anti-HBc IgM, HSV), drugs (anti-TB drugs, herbal/ayurvedic), autoimmune, Wilson (age < 40), Budd-Chiari (Doppler), pregnancy (AFLP/HELLP), mushroom.

steps.title: Specific treatments
steps.detail: NAC for paracetamol; NAC for early-grade non-paracetamol ALF; antivirals for HBV; delivery for AFLP/HELLP; acyclovir for HSV; steroids for autoimmune (selected).

steps.title: Contact a transplant centre early
steps.detail: Discuss every ALF with encephalopathy or INR > 2 with a liver transplant unit; apply King's College criteria serially.

steps.title: Neuroprotection
steps.detail: Intubate grade III-IV HE; head-up 30°, normocapnia, Na 140-150 mmol/L (hypertonic saline), treat fever; mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg or hypertonic saline for ICP surges. Ammonia > 150-200 µmol/L = high risk of cerebral oedema.

steps.title: Organ support
steps.detail: Noradrenaline for MAP ≥ 65 mmHg after fluids; early CRRT for hyperammonaemia, AKI or fluid/acid-base problems; glucose 4-hourly (dextrose infusion for hypoglycaemia); low threshold for antibiotics/antifungals.

steps.title: Coagulation
steps.detail: Do not correct INR prophylactically (it is a prognostic marker); vitamin K 10 mg IV once; products only for bleeding or procedures.

steps.title: Plasma exchange
steps.detail: High-volume plasma exchange (8-12 L or 15% of ideal body weight per day for 3 days) improved transplant-free survival; consider as bridge in specialist centres.

doseCards.dose: 150 mg/kg/h × 1 h, 12.5 mg/kg/h × 4 h, then 6.25 mg/kg/h × 67 h
doseCards.dilution: Each phase in 5% dextrose (e.g. load in 250 mL, then 500 mL, then 1,000 mL bags)
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 10.5 g over 1 h, then 875 mg/h for 4 h, then 437.5 mg/h for 67 h

tables.title: King's College criteria (transplant referral)
rows: Arterial pH < 7.30 after fluid resuscitation, OR all of: INR > 6.5, creatinine > 3.4 mg/dL (300 µmol/L), grade III-IV HE within 24 h
Lactate > 3.5 mmol/L at 4 h or > 3.0 mmol/L after fluid resuscitation adds sensitivity

INR > 6.5, OR any 3 of: age < 10 or > 40 years; aetiology non-A non-B hepatitis, halothane or idiosyncratic drug reaction; jaundice-to-HE interval > 7 days; INR > 3.5; bilirubin > 17.5 mg/dL (300 µmol/L)
tables.caption: Low sensitivity: absence of criteria does not guarantee survival. Clichy criteria (factor V) are an alternative.

redFlags.text: Rising ammonia (> 150-200 µmol/L), grade III-IV HE, pupillary changes, hypertension with bradycardia: impending intracranial hypertension.
Hypoglycaemia is common and can mimic worsening encephalopathy: check glucose every 1-4 h.

pitfalls.text: Giving FFP to 'correct' INR: masks prognosis, adds volume and rarely needed.
Sedating with benzodiazepines; use propofol/short-acting opioids once intubated.
Missing hepatitis E in pregnancy and anti-TB DILI in India.

pearls.text: Sequential lactate, INR trend and HE grade guide referral better than a single value.

nodes.text: Intubate; ICP-protective care; Na 140-150; CRRT if ammonia high
HDU/ICU: glucose 1-4 hourly, avoid sedatives, monitor
Super-urgent transplant listing; HVPE as bridge
Continue support; reassess criteria every 12-24 h

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Massive hepatocyte necrosis/apoptosis causes loss of synthetic, metabolic and detoxifying function. Ammonia is converted to glutamine in astrocytes, causing swelling and cerebral oedema; systemic inflammation produces vasodilatory shock and multi-organ failure resembling sepsis.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- EASL 2017 ALF guideline covers aetiology, intensive care and transplant criteria [EASL 2017].
- Lee 2009: NAC improved transplant-free survival in non-paracetamol ALF with grade I-II HE (52% vs 30%), not in grade III-IV [Lee 2009].
- Larsen 2016: high-volume plasma exchange improved transplant-free survival (58.7% vs 47.8%) [Larsen 2016].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Routine ICP monitoring; prophylactic hypothermia (no benefit in trials); prophylactic antimicrobials.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- In India, viral hepatitis (HEV, HAV, HBV) and drug-induced liver injury (especially anti-TB drugs and complementary medicines) predominate; paracetamol ALF is uncommon.
- HEV-related ALF in pregnancy carries high mortality.
- Indian prognostic models (e.g. ALFED) are used in some centres; living-donor liver transplant is the predominant transplant type in India, which affects timing.

topics.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure
topics.summary: Define ACLF (EASL-CLIF and APASL), treat precipitants including alcoholic hepatitis and HBV flare, support organs, and decide on transplant or futility.

definition.text: ACLF is acute decompensation of chronic liver disease with organ failures and high short-term mortality. EASL-CLIF: graded 1-3 by organ failures (CLIF-C OF score). APASL: jaundice (bilirubin ≥ 5 mg/dL) and coagulopathy (INR ≥ 1.5) complicated within 4 weeks by ascites and/or HE.

steps.title: Identify precipitant
steps.detail: Infection (SBP, pneumonia, UTI), alcoholic hepatitis, HBV reactivation/flare, HEV/HAV superinfection, DILI, GI bleed. Culture all sites, diagnostic paracentesis.

steps.title: Grade
steps.detail: Count organ failures (liver, kidney, brain, coagulation, circulation, respiration) using CLIF-C OF; calculate CLIF-C ACLF score or APASL AARC score.

steps.title: Treat infection early
steps.detail: Empirical antibiotics according to local resistance (nosocomial: broader cover); start within 1 h if septic shock.

steps.title: Alcoholic hepatitis
steps.detail: Maddrey DF ≥ 32 or MELD > 20 without infection/bleeding/AKI: prednisolone 40 mg/day; Lille at day 7 (≥ 0.45 = stop). Abstinence counselling.

steps.title: HBV
steps.detail: Start tenofovir or entecavir immediately in HBV-related ACLF.

steps.title: Organ support
steps.detail: Albumin for volume, noradrenaline ± terlipressin, CRRT, ventilation; HE care; avoid nephrotoxins and sedatives.

steps.title: Transplant evaluation
steps.detail: Early referral; ACLF-2/3 have 28-day mortality 30-80% without transplant.

steps.title: Reassess at day 3-7
steps.detail: If ≥ 4 organ failures or CLIF-C ACLF > 70 after 3-7 days of full support and not a transplant candidate, discuss limitation/palliation.

doseCards.dose: Tenofovir DF 300 mg daily (or entecavir 0.5 mg daily)

tables.title: EASL-CLIF ACLF grades (simplified)
rows: None, or single non-kidney OF with creatinine < 1.5 and no HE
Single kidney failure, or single other OF with creatinine 1.5-1.9 mg/dL and/or grade I-II HE

redFlags.text: ACLF-3, particularly with ≥ 4 organ failures persisting after 3-7 days: very high mortality without transplant.

pitfalls.text: Starting steroids for alcoholic hepatitis without excluding infection.
Applying APASL and EASL definitions interchangeably: they select different populations.

pearls.text: Each additional organ failure markedly increases mortality; count organ failures daily.

nodes.text: Count organ failures; CLIF-C ACLF / AARC score

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Systemic inflammation driven by PAMPs (infection, translocation) and DAMPs (alcohol, viral hepatitis) causes immunopathology, mitochondrial dysfunction and organ failure on a background of portal hypertension and immune paresis.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- EASL 2023 ACLF guideline: definitions, organ support, transplant and futility [EASL 2023].
- APASL 2019 update, with AARC score widely used in Asia [Sarin 2019].
- Lille model: non-response to steroids (≥ 0.45) predicts poor survival [Louvet 2007].
consultantNotes.controversies: - G-CSF, plasma exchange and extracorporeal liver support in ACLF; transplant in ACLF-3.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- APASL criteria were developed largely from Asian (including Indian) cohorts with alcohol and HBV/HEV precipitants.
- Cost of transplant and limited deceased-donor organs mean early goals-of-care discussions are important in India.

options: Bilirubin ≥ 5 mg/dL and INR ≥ 1.5 with ascites/HE within 4 weeks

topics.title: Hepatic encephalopathy
topics.summary: Grade HE, find and treat precipitants, give lactulose (or PEG), add rifaximin, protect the airway and keep feeding.

definition.text: HE is brain dysfunction due to liver insufficiency and/or portosystemic shunting. West Haven grades: I (trivial lack of awareness, short attention), II (lethargy, disorientation, asterixis), III (somnolence, confusion, responsive to stimuli), IV (coma).

steps.title: Exclude other causes
steps.detail: Hypoglycaemia, sepsis, hyponatraemia, intracranial bleed (CT if focal signs or fall), alcohol withdrawal, Wernicke, drugs. A normal ammonia should prompt a search for another diagnosis.

steps.title: Treat precipitants
steps.detail: Infection, GI bleeding, constipation, dehydration/over-diuresis, hypokalaemia, sedatives/opioids, TIPS, AKI.

steps.title: Airway
steps.detail: Grade III-IV: nurse in HDU/ICU; intubate if unable to protect airway (GCS ≤ 8) or for endoscopy.

steps.title: Lactulose
steps.detail: 25-30 mL every 1-2 h until bowel motion, then titrate to 2-3 soft stools/day. Via NG or enema if unable to swallow.

steps.title: PEG 3350 alternative
steps.detail: 4 L PEG over 4 h resolved HE faster than lactulose in HELP; consider when lactulose fails (airway risk).

steps.title: Rifaximin
steps.detail: Add 550 mg BD for recurrent HE (secondary prophylaxis with lactulose).

steps.title: Nutrition
steps.detail: Do not restrict protein: 1.2-1.5 g/kg/day, energy 35 kcal/kg/day, late evening snack; enteral feeding if unable to eat.

steps.title: Refractory
steps.detail: Consider LOLA, embolisation of large spontaneous portosystemic shunts, TIPS reduction; transplant evaluation.

doseCards.dose: 25-30 mL every 1-2 h until bowel motion, then titrate to 2-3 stools/day
doseCards.notes: Enema: 300 mL in 700 mL water, retained 30-60 min.

tables.title: West Haven grades
rows: Abnormal psychometrics; mild inattention, sleep inversion
Lethargy, disorientation to time, inappropriate behaviour, asterixis
Somnolent but rousable, gross disorientation, bizarre behaviour

redFlags.text: Focal neurology or head injury in a cirrhotic with confusion: CT head (coagulopathy, falls).

pitfalls.text: Restricting protein: worsens sarcopenia and outcomes.
Excess lactulose causing dehydration, hypernatraemia and AKI.

pearls.text: HE is a clinical diagnosis; ammonia helps mainly by its negative predictive value.

nodes.text: Glucose, Na, sepsis screen, CT if focal/fall
Continue lactulose ± rifaximin; feed 1.2-1.5 g/kg protein
Recheck diagnosis; PEG, rifaximin, LOLA; transplant review

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Gut-derived ammonia bypasses hepatic clearance; astrocytic glutamine accumulation, neuroinflammation, GABA-ergic tone and manganese deposition contribute. Lactulose acidifies the colon (NH3 → NH4+), is cathartic and alters flora.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- EASL 2022 HE guideline [EASL 2022].
- HELP (50 patients): PEG improved HE grade at 24 h more than lactulose [Rahimi 2014].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Routine ammonia measurement; LOLA and branched-chain amino acids.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Lactulose and rifaximin are inexpensive and widely available in India; LOLA is commonly used in Indian practice.

topics.title: Ascites, SBP and hepatorenal syndrome in the ICU
topics.summary: Diagnostic paracentesis in every admission, treat SBP with antibiotics plus albumin, safe large-volume paracentesis, and recognise HRS-AKI.

definition.text: SBP = ascitic neutrophils (PMN) ≥ 250 cells/mm³ without a surgical source. HRS-AKI = AKI (ICA-KDIGO) in cirrhosis with ascites, not responding to 48 h diuretic withdrawal and albumin 1 g/kg, without shock, nephrotoxins or structural kidney disease.

steps.title: Diagnostic paracentesis
steps.detail: In every cirrhotic admitted with ascites, GI bleed, encephalopathy, AKI or infection: cell count, culture in blood-culture bottles at bedside, albumin (SAAG), total protein. Coagulopathy is not a contraindication.

steps.title: Treat SBP
steps.detail: Ceftriaxone 2 g/day or cefotaxime (community); piperacillin-tazobactam or carbapenem (nosocomial/MDR risk) for 5-7 days. Repeat tap at 48 h if not improving (PMN should fall ≥ 25%).

steps.title: Albumin in SBP
steps.detail: 1.5 g/kg on day 1 and 1 g/kg on day 3 (reduces AKI and death), especially if creatinine > 1 mg/dL, bilirubin > 4 mg/dL or urea high.

steps.title: Secondary bacterial peritonitis
steps.detail: Suspect if PMN very high, multiple organisms, total protein > 1 g/dL, glucose < 50 mg/dL, LDH high: CT and surgical review.

steps.title: Large-volume paracentesis
steps.detail: For tense ascites: drain; if > 5 L removed give albumin 6-8 g per litre removed (e.g. 8 L = 48-64 g). Safe without routine FFP/platelets.

steps.title: AKI in cirrhosis
steps.detail: Stop diuretics, NSAIDs, nephrotoxins; treat infection; albumin 1 g/kg (max 100 g) for 2 days; if HRS-AKI criteria met, terlipressin + albumin (see AKI module).

steps.title: Prophylaxis
steps.detail: Long-term norfloxacin/ciprofloxacin after SBP; avoid beta-blocker hypotension in refractory ascites (SBP < 90 mmHg, Na < 130, AKI).

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 105 g (5 × 100 mL of 20%) day 1, 70 g day 3

doseCards.verify: Local resistance; switch for nosocomial SBP.

tables.title: Ascitic fluid interpretation
rows: Protein > 1 g/dL + glucose < 50 mg/dL + LDH > serum ULN

redFlags.text: SBP with rising creatinine: high risk of HRS-AKI and death; give albumin and avoid nephrotoxins.

pitfalls.text: Waiting for culture before treating SBP; culture is negative in ~40% (culture-negative neutrocytic ascites is treated the same).

pearls.text: Inoculating 10 mL of ascitic fluid into blood culture bottles at the bedside increases culture yield.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Splanchnic vasodilation reduces effective arterial volume, activating RAAS, SNS and vasopressin; sodium and water retention cause ascites and dilutional hyponatraemia, and renal vasoconstriction causes HRS. Bacterial translocation underlies SBP.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- Sort 1999: albumin with cefotaxime reduced renal impairment (10% vs 33%) and mortality (10% vs 29%) in SBP [Sort 1999].
- AASLD 2021 and EASL 2018 guidance on ascites, SBP, paracentesis and HRS [Biggins 2021; EASL 2018].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Long-term albumin (ANSWER vs ATTIRE); beta-blockers in refractory ascites.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Tuberculous peritonitis is an important differential in India (ascitic ADA, lymphocytes, SAAG < 1.1).
- High prevalence of ESBL and carbapenem resistance in Indian hospitals means nosocomial SBP often needs a carbapenem; follow local antibiogram (ICMR AMRSN).

topics.title: Coagulopathy in liver disease
topics.summary: Rebalanced haemostasis: why INR misleads, when to give products, viscoelastic testing, and VTE prophylaxis.

definition.text: Chronic liver disease causes 'rebalanced haemostasis': reduced pro- and anticoagulant factors, thrombocytopenia offset by high von Willebrand factor. INR/PT does not predict procedural bleeding and patients remain at risk of thrombosis.

steps.title: Do not correct INR prophylactically
steps.detail: No FFP before low-risk procedures (paracentesis, thoracocentesis, central lines with ultrasound) regardless of INR.

steps.title: High-risk procedures
steps.detail: Assess case by case; viscoelastic tests (TEG/ROTEM) reduce product use. Platelets if < 50 × 10⁹/L for high-risk procedures (or thrombopoietin agonists electively).

steps.title: Active bleeding
steps.detail: Treat portal hypertension first (vasoactive, endoscopy); correct fibrinogen (< 100-120 mg/dL: cryoprecipitate), platelets > 50, guided by viscoelastic testing; restrictive RBC transfusion.

steps.title: Vitamin K
steps.detail: 10 mg IV if cholestasis, malnutrition or antibiotics; little effect in parenchymal failure.

steps.title: Correct triggers
steps.detail: Infection, AKI/uraemia, hypothermia, acidosis and hypocalcaemia worsen bleeding.

steps.title: VTE prophylaxis
steps.detail: Give LMWH prophylaxis to immobile cirrhotic ICU patients without active bleeding or very low platelets; a high INR is not protective.

doseCards.verify: Fibrinogen per unit varies by blood bank.

redFlags.text: Unexplained bleeding with hyperfibrinolysis (oozing from puncture sites, ROTEM lysis): consider tranexamic acid after specialist input.

pitfalls.text: Giving 4 units of FFP before an ascitic tap: no benefit, volume overload and higher portal pressure.

pearls.text: Portal vein thrombosis is common in cirrhosis; check Doppler in decompensation.

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Reduced synthesis of factors II, V, VII, IX, X, XI and of protein C/S and antithrombin, with high factor VIII and vWF and low ADAMTS13, produces a fragile balance that can tip to bleeding (infection, uraemia) or thrombosis.
consultantNotes.evidence: - EASL 2022 bleeding and thrombosis guideline: avoid prophylactic correction of INR; use viscoelastic testing; give VTE prophylaxis [EASL 2022].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Platelet and fibrinogen thresholds before high-risk procedures.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- TEG/ROTEM are available mainly in tertiary centres; where unavailable, fibrinogen level and platelet count guide therapy.
- Cryoprecipitate and single-donor platelets are often available only in blood banks of larger hospitals.

options: Give vitamin K and wait 24 h

drugs.name: N-acetylcysteine
drugs.indications: Paracetamol hepatotoxicity; early-grade (I-II HE) non-paracetamol ALF
drugs.adultDose: Non-paracetamol ALF (Lee 2009): 150 mg/kg/h for 1 h, then 12.5 mg/kg/h for 4 h, then 6.25 mg/kg/h for 67 h (72 h total). Paracetamol: 21-h regimen 150 mg/kg over 1 h, 50 mg/kg over 4 h, 100 mg/kg over 16 h; continue 6.25 mg/kg/h if ALF.
drugs.preparationIndia: 200 mg/mL (Indian vials 1 g/5 mL and 2 g/10 mL); dilute in 5% dextrose.
drugs.cautions: Anaphylactoid reactions (flushing, bronchospasm) mostly during loading; slow or pause, give antihistamine. Fluid load in small patients.
drugs.verify: Weight cap (commonly 100-110 kg) and local NAC protocol.

drugs.name: Vitamin K1 (phytomenadione)
drugs.indications: Possible vitamin K deficiency (cholestasis, malnutrition, antibiotics)
drugs.adultDose: 10 mg IV slowly once (repeat daily for 3 days if response).

drugs.name: Prednisolone
drugs.indications: Severe alcoholic hepatitis (Maddrey DF ≥ 32 or MELD > 20) without contraindication
drugs.adultDose: 40 mg orally once daily for 28 days; stop at day 7 if Lille score ≥ 0.45.
drugs.cautions: Exclude/treat infection, GI bleed, AKI first; risk of infection.

drugs.name: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate / entecavir
drugs.adultDose: Tenofovir DF 300 mg orally once daily (or entecavir 0.5 mg daily); adjust for renal function.

drugs.name: Lactulose
drugs.indications: Hepatic encephalopathy treatment and secondary prophylaxis
drugs.adultDose: 25-30 mL (oral/NG) every 1-2 h until a bowel motion, then titrate to 2-3 soft stools/day (usually 15-30 mL two to three times daily). Enema 300 mL in 700 mL water if NG not possible.
drugs.cautions: Over-use causes dehydration, hypernatraemia, hypokalaemia and can worsen HE/AKI.

drugs.name: Rifaximin
drugs.adultDose: 550 mg orally twice daily (or 400 mg three times daily).
drugs.preparationIndia: 400 mg and 550 mg tablets available in India.

drugs.name: Polyethylene glycol 3350-electrolyte
drugs.adultDose: 4 L over 4 h orally or by NG (single dose) (HELP trial).
drugs.cautions: Aspiration risk in encephalopathic patients; give via NG with airway protection if needed.

drugs.name: Human albumin 20%
drugs.adultDose: SBP: 1.5 g/kg day 1 and 1 g/kg day 3 (max ~100 g/day). LVP > 5 L: 6-8 g per litre removed. HRS-AKI: 1 g/kg (max 100 g) day 1-2, then 20-40 g/day with terlipressin.
drugs.cautions: Pulmonary oedema, especially with terlipressin; monitor lungs/POCUS.

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.indications: Community-acquired SBP; GI bleed prophylaxis in cirrhosis
drugs.adultDose: SBP: 2 g IV once daily for 5-7 days (or cefotaxime 2 g q8h). Use piperacillin-tazobactam or carbapenem for nosocomial SBP or high-MDR settings.

drugs.name: Cryoprecipitate
drugs.indications: Bleeding with fibrinogen < 100-120 mg/dL in liver disease
drugs.adultDose: 1 unit per 10 kg (about 8-10 units adult) or per viscoelastic test.
drugs.verify: Fibrinogen content per unit varies by blood bank.
